description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'owed-null-placeholder-name'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: THE CONTROL, and it is not decoration: the refusal row below carries this same placeholder map plus a null key, so without this row a port that refused EVERY placeholder map would pass the refusal and look correct.

DefaultStrings:690. Java snapshots the caller's placeholder map and refuses a null KEY before any lookup runs. Plan 3.2 types Placeholders as `Record<string, unknown> | ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>` and blesses the Map form for generated or untrusted keys, so a null key is an ordinary caller shape on this side too -- and it is exactly the shape a generated key list produces when one entry is missing. FOUND A REAL PORT DEFECT: lokalized-js answered 'Hello world', silently ignoring the null-named entry, which is the behaviour the disposition for this branch predicted.
